title: Insect life
intro: Hi again! Now we'll see where insects live, how they find a mate and how they grow. You'll see that a caterpillar and a butterfly are the same animal.

lessons.title: Where they live
lessons.intro: Insects are almost everywhere. Let's find out where they live and why they can live there.
lessons.closing: Insects live in almost every ecosystem because they adapt, they are small and many can fly. Where there are plants, there is food for them.

exercises.prompt: Where can insects live?
options: Almost everywhere: deserts, forests, rivers and even snowy mountains
exercises.explanation: They live in almost every land ecosystem, from deserts to snowy peaks.

exercises.prompt: Why can they live in so many places?
options: Because they adapt and many can fly
exercises.explanation: Their ability to adapt, their flight and their small size help them get everywhere.

exercises.prompt: Match each insect with the place where you can find it.
exercises.explanation: Each insect lives where it finds what it needs: food, water and shelter.

exercises.prompt: Where are insects most common?
options: In places with no plants at all
exercises.explanation: Where there are leaves, seeds, fruit and nectar, there is food for them.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: Some insects live in ___ water like rivers, lakes and streams.
exercises.explanation: Freshwater insects only come out when they need to breathe.

lessons.title: How they find a mate
lessons.intro: Insects live a short time and reproduce quickly. To find each other they use light, sounds, scents and even dances.
lessons.closing: Insects communicate in amazing ways: with light, music and smells. Watching them quietly is the best way to see it.

exercises.prompt: How do fireflies communicate to find each other?
exercises.explanation: Fireflies give off light to call each other.

exercises.prompt: Match each insect with how it communicates.

pairs.right: Its scent travels through the air
Rubs its legs against its wings and sings

exercises.explanation: Scent, music, light and strength: each one has its own way.

exercises.prompt: How does a male grasshopper "sing"?
options: By rubbing its back legs against its wings
exercises.explanation: It rubs its back legs against its wings to make a song and court.

exercises.prompt: How do male butterflies find the females?
options: By following their scent in the air
By the sound of their wings
exercises.explanation: The females give off a scent and the males follow its trail in the air.

exercises.prompt: Insects live a short time. That's why they reproduce...
exercises.explanation: Their life is short, so they reproduce quickly.

lessons.title: Complete metamorphosis
lessons.intro: A caterpillar looks nothing like a butterfly, but it's the same animal! Let's see how it changes.
lessons.closing: In complete metamorphosis the insect changes completely, like the butterfly. While it is in the chrysalis it doesn't eat or move: it is transforming.

exercises.prompt: Put the butterfly's life cycle in order.
exercises.explanation: Egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa (chrysalis) and adult butterfly.

exercises.prompt: What is the stage between the larva and the adult called?
exercises.explanation: The change happens inside the chrysalis, also called the pupa.

exercises.prompt: Most insects start life as...
exercises.explanation: Almost all start as an egg.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: Egg, larva, ___ and adult: that's complete metamorphosis.
exercises.explanation: The pupa is the chrysalis.

exercises.prompt: How long can it take a larva to become an adult?
exercises.explanation: It depends on the insect: it can take several weeks or even years.

lessons.title: Incomplete metamorphosis
lessons.intro: Other insects don't make a chrysalis: they hatch looking almost like their parents and keep growing. Let's see!
lessons.closing: In incomplete metamorphosis the young are nymphs, small versions of their parents. They grow by changing their exoskeleton, like changing clothes that got too small.

exercises.prompt: Put the grasshopper's life cycle in order.
exercises.explanation: Egg, nymph and adult grasshopper: no chrysalis.

exercises.prompt: What are the young called in incomplete metamorphosis?
exercises.explanation: They are called nymphs.

exercises.prompt: A nymph is...
options: A miniature version of its parents
exercises.explanation: It looks like its parents, but smaller and almost always without wings.

exercises.prompt: How does a nymph grow?
options: By eating leaves from another plant
exercises.explanation: When it gets too small, it changes its exoskeleton: this is called molting.

exercises.prompt: Match each type of metamorphosis with what identifies it.

pairs.right: Goes through a chrysalis or pupa

exercises.explanation: Complete: with a pupa. Incomplete: with a nymph.

exam.title: Unit challenge
exam.intro: Another challenge! Ten mixed questions about insect life. If you pass, you open the next unit.
exam.closing: Now you know where insects live, how they find each other and how they grow! A forest ranger watches without disturbing.

exercises.explanation: Scent, music and light.

exercises.explanation: Egg, larva, pupa and adult.

exercises.explanation: Nymph.

exercises.explanation: Fresh water.

exercises.prompt: How does a male grasshopper "sing"?
options: By rubbing its back legs against its wings
exercises.explanation: It rubs its legs and wings.

exercises.prompt: Put the grasshopper's life cycle in order.
exercises.explanation: Egg, nymph and adult.

exercises.prompt: Inside the chrysalis, the insect...
exercises.explanation: It changes from larva to adult.

exercises.prompt: Most insects start life as...
exercises.explanation: Egg.

exercises.prompt: How does a nymph grow?
exercises.explanation: By molting.
